The second-map test (2026-11-10), the harness's seventh program: the recipes that finished surf_src_sidistic from scratch in the one-search series (~/ar_az) run UNCHANGED on surf_princessburglar_b26. CLAUDE.md 0b: a winner is called only when the SAME recipe repeats on a second map with no constant changed. Operator-run, no agents and no orchestrator: a frozen recipe leaves nothing to design. Two arms, one seed each, from scratch at the true start: m2sib (branch m2/sib = azr1b2_pool's commit 4644510b: one pool of spawns + the sibling-yield mix rule in the tree search; sidistic first finish 7.248B steps) and m2pool (branch m2/pool = azr1b1_pool1's commit da7981e5: one pool, the search at the random end; sidistic first finish 14.194B). Every number here is a HARD limit that box.py and the watchdog enforce.
goal: Does the recipe that finishes sidistic also finish surf_src_cannonball (a long descent whose field has one known barrier: the final descent raises the distance by about 8,400 u at 88.8% of the route) from the true start, champion-free, with no flag or constant changed? Read by finishes inside the real finish trigger and the step of the first finishing eval; without a finish, by where the greedy policy stops (tools/eval_honesty.py corridor MAX, measurement only: race/eval_progress saturates at the wall). The cannonball numbers in CLAUDE.md (97k gate at 0.5-1.0B steps, the 205k wall at 1.0-1.75B, 0 finishes in 2.0B from scratch) are a bar to read against, never a constant.
_field_doc: surf_src_cannonball's goal graph WITHOUT corner cutting at lidar cell 32, the field the recipe shapes on (--race-no-corner-cut 1). The user's cannonball_maps.tar.gz (md5 394b7cd5, brought from the user's PC 2026-11-11 07:03 UTC) carries bsp, zones, goal_32, occ_32, sdf_32, slabocc_32 and faceid_32 but no goalc_32, and the droplet CPU is taken by a measurement queue, so the field is baked ON THE BOX before the launch (tools/bake_nocut_field.py --device cuda), pulled back md5-verified and added to ~/ar_m2/maps/cannonballc_maps.tar.gz; the trainer and score.py then read one field. PROVISIONAL until that bake: start_d and start_d_span below are read off the shipped corner-cutting goal_32 at the 4 spawn points (198,352 .. 198,416 u).
_score_episodes_doc: score.py counts only the first N episodes of an eval (header episode index < N): its score is a max over episodes, so an eval with more episodes would buy lottery tickets (r6b1 scored 98.418 with 54-episode evals of the incumbent's weights). 0 = all.
_rounds_doc: The user, 2026-11-10 11:31 UTC, on the one-search series: 'I think we can call it. Let's wrap it up, and then start the methods that did converge on other map. E.g. princessburglar'. No orchestrator runs here; round_hours / rounds are unused.
_max_boxes_doc: One box per arm (box.py allows one per 'agent' name): m4sib is the only one planned on this branch. The m2 arms (m2sib, m2pool, m2warm, m2ge) and m3sib are all released. The droplet's ONE fleet watchdog daemon enforces its own cap; boxes are registered in its registry (RLSURF_FLEET_DIR=~/ar/fleet).
_budget_end_hours_doc: Hours from this program's start (state.json started) over which box.py spreads the credit above the reserve: ~$11.5 above the $10 reserve at the start = two fast boxes for about 14 h. No top-ups by the operator.
_max_dph_doc: $/h for the WHOLE box, its disk_gb of storage included: box.py prices offers with --storage disk_gb, and the fleet watchdog checks the instance's dph_total against its own caps (this table is a subset of them). FAST cards first in this program, because a 26 h round is read in steps: measured on the recipe last round, RTX 5080 368k steps/s, RTX 4080 282k, RTX 3090 215k, RTX 5060 Ti 125-179k (the host CPU is half of it). So tier 0 is the 5080 class, then the 3090s, then two 16 GB fallbacks, then a 4090 or 5090 at its old cap; the 4070 / 3080 / 5060 class of 2026-10-25 is out (10B steps in 20 h would not reach the late walls). Caps sit just above the market of 2026-11-09 (5080 0.28-0.31, 4080S 0.41, 3090 0.29-0.36): a 5080 at 0.59 is double the going rate and is not rented (CLAUDE.md: never rent above the market price).
offer_query: num_gpus=1 cuda_vers>=12.8 reliability>0.98 inet_down>300 rentable=true disk_space>60 cpu_cores_effective>=32 cpu_ghz>=2.5 verified=true gpu_ram>=12
_cpu_exclude_doc: Regexes on the offer's cpu_name. vast's cpu_ghz is the TURBO clock (a Haswell E5-2696 v3 lists 3.8 GHz), so it does not catch old server parts: box 56818837, a 3090 on dual Xeon E5-2699 v3 (72 threads, Haswell 2014), trained the incumbent recipe at 57-59k steps/s with the trainer at 5,400% CPU and the GPU 5% busy, against 166-269k on 32-thread Zen 3 / Zen 4 / Raptor Lake hosts (2026-10-20).
_harness_files_doc: The operator's files: at the start of every round orchestrator.py restores them from the main checkout's HEAD over the winner's head, so a branch cannot carry its own caps, grader or rules forward, and the operator's fixes reach every round. autoresearch/NOTES.md is NOT one of them: it is the lineage's memory and travels with the winner. tools/bad_hosts.json is merged instead (the union of every branch's list).
_lineage_keys_doc: Keys of this file that belong to the lineage, not the operator: when the winner changed one during its round, its value travels into the next round's config.json (r1b1 made its scratch recipe the incumbent_recipe on 2026-10-20). Everything else here is restored from the operator's HEAD.
_start_d_span_doc: score.py: the field at the map's 4 spawn points (x -14400 .. -14224, y 3079, z 10528 / 10532). PROVISIONAL (corner-cutting goal_32: 198,352 .. 198,416 u, a spread of 0.03%); replaced by the goalc_32 values after the bake on the box. Evals draw a spawn point per episode, so the 2% start test is taken outside this span. Grader only: nothing in training reads it.
_offer_query_doc: Scratch training here is CPU-bound: the trainer takes half the container's CPUs for physics. A 16-thread 3090 box ran the incumbent recipe at ~36k steps/s (2026-10-20, smoke_x1) against ~420k on the 5090 PC, so boxes need >= 32 effective threads on a fast CPU. Measured the same night on a 3090 + Ryzen 9 5950X box (32 threads, quota 30.7 CPUs, omp 15): ~194k steps/s, GPU 30% busy. gpu_ram>=12 (GB; 2026-10-25): the cheaper cards' 8 GB variants are out, every good card has 16-24 GB.
_incumbent_recipe_doc: The flag list BOTH finishing sidistic runs were launched with (box.log 2026-11-09 20:47:43 azr1b1_pool1 and 2026-11-10 01:58:26 azr1b2_pool, identical up to the last argument), minus that last argument, which the arm passes itself: --auto-spine-mcts-args '--mcts-mix-rule sib --mcts-mix-floor 0.05 --mcts-mix-horizon 256 --mcts-mix-warm 2'. EVERY token is sidistic's, --maxvel 4000 included (the princessburglar arms ran --maxvel 3500, that map's server physics; tools/run_arm.sh pins 4000 on every scratch run and every cannonball run in the ledger used it). The list is byte-identical to the blue200 run's. Launch: box.py launch --agent m4sib --run m4sib_cb --steps 60e9 -- --auto-spine-mcts-args '<the string above>'.
_agent_prefix_doc: Box owner m4sib, run m4sib_cb (cannonball = the fourth map; blue200 was m3sib on branch m3/sib). New names, so no other program's run is ever read as one of these.
_budget_doc: No budget_rate_usd_h: box.py's pacer. The reserve is held by extend's burn x hours check and by the box deadlines.
_time_cap_s_doc: score.py's time term is 10 * (1 - best_finish_s / time_cap_s): 300 s, the episode cap.
